title: Terms
summary: One word for each concept, in the interface, the agents' instructions and the spec.
description:
The words the app and the spec use for its concepts: each term's value is the word, its description the definition.

A description's last sentence, "Not: a, b.", lists the words that term rules out, which the spec check looks for.

stories.as: a learner reading the app and its guide
stories.want: each thing called by one name everywhere
stories.soThat: I never wonder whether two words mean two things

requirements.text: The interface calls each concept by its term, and never by a word the term rules out.
The instructions and tool descriptions given to the tutor, the examiner and the writing partner use the same terms.
The build fails when a requirement, story, summary or description of the spec uses a word a term rules out.

values.description: A folder on one theme that lists lessons in order, and can be completed, mastered and closed.
The unit of learning: one job, of one lesson type, in exactly one course, with its own schedule and mastery points. Not: block.
Which of `lesson.types` a lesson is, which decides how it is practised and what its page shows.
A lesson tapped through as cards over the few words, sentences or dialogue it owns, graded by the share answered right.
One step of a drill: something to read, answer, say or play.
A course's short everyday exchange in Polish, and the drill that practises it. Not: today's conversation.
A study, listening or writing lesson, practised as an exchange with an AI that ends in a verdict; one go at it is a conversation.
The AI that questions the learner in a study or listening lesson and gives the verdict.
The AI that plays a writing lesson's situation with the learner, writing only Polish, and gives the verdict.
A lesson's return on its schedule, whatever its type; a go at a conversation lesson is a conversation, not a check-in.
A go at a lesson already passed today: it pays half XP and leaves the schedule as it was.
A graded go that is good enough, by a drill's score or a conversation's verdict; shown as Passed.
A graded go short of a pass that is not a fail; shown as Partly there. Not: near miss.
A graded go below a partial; shown as Not yet.
A pass with every scored card fully right, or a conversation passed with nothing to go over again.
An answer one slip off, a typed word one letter off or a sentence with one word wrong, which counts as half right. Not: nearly right.
A lesson's points from 0 to `mastery.full`, earned by passing, each change kept with its reason.
Of a lesson, passed and at `mastery.full` mastery points, for good; of a course, completed with every lesson mastered.
Of a course, every core lesson passed once.
A lesson of a course that is not a challenge; in a course of challenges only, every lesson.
A lesson marked as beyond its course's level, explained as `lesson.challenge-explained`.
Of a mastered course, closed by the learner as a trophy: listed under Mastered, never due, and never changed again.
The few lessons chosen each day as the ones that matter most, at the top of Exercises. Not: daily list, daily five, day's list.
The one folder, at the bottom of the course list, for lessons that fit no course; it is never completed or closed.
A mastered lesson whose words are due, given a spare place in today's lessons without risk to its mastery.
Points paid for practice that was really done, counted by day.
The number of done days in a row.
Earned every seventh day of a streak, it covers a missed day by itself.
A minute's play over words already met, outside today's lessons, that moves no schedule.
The AI in the Tutor tab that explains Polish and makes and changes courses, lessons and songs with its tools.
A phone or computer with the app and the learner's data.
The devices that sync one learner's data with each other. Not: vault.
